recent_candidates.title: ¿Se encamina Europa hacia una nueva crisis energética este invierno?
recent_candidates.author: Marin Saillofest
recent_candidates.excerpt: El vórtice polar estratosférico, una vasta circulación invernal que se extiende sobre cada uno de los polos, suele desintegrarse a finales de enero. Este año, varios modelos meteorológicos indican que podría colapsar ya en los próximos días, lo que lo convertiría en el colapso más precoz jamás registrado y podría provocar, en las semanas siguientes, una afluencia de aire ártico hacia Norteamérica y Europa 91 . Una ola de frío precoz podría afectar a las reservas europeas de gas natural, que se encuentran en su nivel más bajo en esta época del año desde que Gas Infrastructure Europe (GIE) comenzara a recopilar datos en 2011. A 1 de noviembre, las capacidades de almacenamiento de la Unión solo estaban ocupadas en un 74,6%, frente al 82,8% del año pasado y al 95,2% de 2024. En un informe publicado hoy, martes 3 de noviembre, la Agencia Internacional de la Energía estima que unas temperaturas invernales más frías de lo habitual en Europa, junto con un cierre del estrecho de Ormuz hasta finales de marzo, podrían aumentar el consumo de gas en los edificios en más de un 10%, y en un 7% en el sector eléctrico entre noviembre y marzo, en comparación con el invierno pasado 92 . En la industria, los elevados precios provocarían un descenso del 15% en el consumo, lo que supondría una caída de la demanda similar a la registrada durante la crisis energética de 2022-2023, tras la invasión rusa de Ucrania. recent_candidates.excerpt: Hoy, martes 3 de noviembre, se someterán a votación más de 40 propuestas de referéndum relacionadas con la construcción de centros de datos en 10 estados. recent_candidates.author: J.D. Capelouto

recent_candidates.title: FDA grants tentative approval to low-cost HIV shot
recent_candidates.author: Jeronimo Gonzalez
recent_candidates.excerpt: US regulators’ approval of a cheaper HIV shot has lifted hopes in some of the world’s poorest countries, many of which are reeling from Western aid cuts. The FDA granted tentative approval of a generic lenacapavir, a twice-a-year injection that helps prevent HIV infection. The move will make the drug available for $40 per person a year in 120 low- and middle-income countries, the Associated Press reported. Washington’s funding cuts to some HIV-prevention programs in Africa left efforts there floundering, sparking fears that the continent could see hundreds of thousands of additional deaths from AIDS. A large-scale rollout of the affordable drug could help “ bring an end to the HIV epidemic ,” a global health advocate said. — Jeronimo Gonzalez

recent_candidates.title: Cyberattacks in Europe target supermarkets, blood banks
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: Another wave of cyberattacks against European supermarkets this week compromised refrigeration systems for the second time in a month, rekindling fears over the security of critical infrastructure. While such attacks so far have been costly and inconvenient , a new era of AI-enabled cyberwarfare could portend more devastating disruptions. France’s national blood service, which 1,900 hospitals rely on, said Tuesday that hackers raised the temperature at cold storage units , but the attack was thwarted before any damage was done . Experts frequently blame Russia for such incidents: Many Kremlin-aligned hacks are unsophisticated, but “the problem is that the more they poke around, the more it is probable they can find something critical that wasn’t protected well ,” a cyber analyst said. — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: Midterm defeat deals death blow to Trump coalition
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: A historic Democratic rout sounded the death knell for the Trump coalition, commentators argued. Republicans’ midterm wipeout on Tuesday marks the end of a nationalist movement based on “ projecting invulnerability and ruthlessness ,” Politico wrote, to which “so many executives and diplomats and generals and prime ministers chose to submit.” Still, the results don’t guarantee years of Democratic dominance: Swing voters are “ leasing one-year terms ,” journalist Derek Thompson wrote, making Tuesday less a realignment than a “historic collapse.” President Donald Trump’s once-successful strategy of turning out his base “with money from people who didn’t understand that base” didn’t work this time, Semafor’s David Weigel argued: “Democrats made a bet that gravity was real, and Trump couldn’t defy it anymore .” — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: Iran takes credit for handing Trump a midterm defeat
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: Republicans’ resounding defeat Tuesday prompted quiet jubilation in Europe and exultation in Iran, as foreign capitals sized up a domestically constrained White House. Tehran took credit for handing US President Donald Trump “a strategic defeat on the battlefield… and a POLITICAL DEFEAT in Washington ,” following reports that Iranian negotiators stalled talks to keep US gas prices high. Washington’s European allies, who have navigated two years of friction with the US over military funding, the Ukraine war , and Greenland, were largely silent, though Italy’s former prime minister said “Europe is much stronger” thanks to the “blue wave.” Others were less sanguine. Trump is “quite weakened,” France’s economy minister acknowledged, but noted that the “unpredictable” president remains “ in charge of international policy .” — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: Republicans trade blame for historic midterm loss
recent_candidates.author: Brendan Ruberry
recent_candidates.excerpt: The Republicans’ devastating midterm losses prompted heated recriminations, as well as unofficial campaigning for the 2028 GOP presidential nomination. President Donald Trump insisted he “wasn’t on the ticket,” after weeks of urging voters to “pretend I’m on the ballot.” A defiant White House was quick to pin blame on the losing candidates , who in turn pointed fingers at the president’s tariff policies and his unpopular war with Iran: Trump was “ the engineer of the Republican collapse ,” a GOP strategist told The New York Times. Prominent Republicans like Florida’s governor called for a reckoning , and early presidential frontrunner Vice President JD Vance earned plaudits for declaring that the Iran war was the “ real reason ” for Tuesday’s losses. — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: A consumer-based AI wave is coming
recent_candidates.author: Reed Albergotti
recent_candidates.excerpt: The bulk of investment in the AI boom has gone into enterprise applications — that is, technology that people use for work. But the biggest successes in the tech industry that have carried the entire stock market for decades have almost all started with consumers. Marissa Mayer, who recently started a consumer AI app called Dazzle and joined me on Semafor’s Future Proof, says thatby 2030, consumer AI will be about twice the size of enterprise. Dazzle, an AI personal assistant that doesn’t read your email or calendar like other AI productivity apps, looks almost exclusively at your photo reel to gain information about you. Its capabilities are impressive considering its narrow source of data. And whether it goes on to become a fixture in AI’s future, it is a preview of a new consumer-focused tech wave that hasn’t yet arrived in the industry. Once it does, the public’s perception of AI could change again. Based on Tuesday’s election results, it’s hard to imagine it could get worse. — Reed Albergotti

recent_candidates.excerpt: If there is one thing that educated people on either side of the Atlantic think they know, it is that the United States has a constitution and the United Kingdom does not. The better-informed might aver that Britain has only an unwritten constitution, the principles of which are disputed or at least open to a wide range of interpretations. In fact, nobody has even attempted to describe these principles since the Victorian era, when Walter Bagehot and A. V. Dicey sought to codify the British constitution, with only partial success. A more recent volume of guidance compiled by Whitehall civil servants, the semi-official Cabinet Manual , has been honoured by ministers as much in the breach as in the observance—but in any case it has no statutory authority. Even if it did, Parliament could alter or abolish it at any time. Ever since England’s first written quasi-constitution—the 1653 Instrument of Government which created Oliver Cromwell’s Protectorate but lasted only four years before being superseded—there have been documents that might have evolved into genuine constitutional frameworks. Yet even those that have acquired permanent symbolic status, such as the 1689 Bill of Rights, are still subject to the interpretative vagaries of the zeitgeist. Last spring, Minnesota’s legislature, in a nearly unanimous vote, passed HF 1606 , titled “Prohibition on Nudification Technology.” The law enables the state attorney general to seek up to $500,000 in fines from a technology company each time that company allows “a user to access, download, or use the website, application, software, program, or other service to nudify an image or video” or to “nudify an image or video on behalf of a user.” The law broadly defines “nudify” as altering or generating a video or image “to depict an intimate part not depicted in an original unaltered image or video of an identifiable individual” provided that the image or video “is so realistic that a reasonable person would believe that the intimate part belongs to the identifiable individual.” Many states—including Minnesota—already have nonconsensual intimate imagery laws , and some of those laws already cover deepfakes. recent_candidates.title: Recuperan las grabaciones más antiguas de una lengua en peligro de extinción en EEUU
recent_candidates.author: Sinc
recent_candidates.excerpt: Las primeras grabaciones conocidas de habla espontánea en criollo de Luisiana , una lengua propia de Estados Unidos en riesgo de extinción, han salido a la luz y han sido analizadas por primera vez. El material permite conocer mejor un idioma que durante más de un siglo caracterizó la vida de los muelles y las tabernas de Nueva Orleans . Las grabaciones de campo, realizadas en 1935 por Lorenzo Dow Turner , un pionero académico afroamericano y lingüista, constituyen un documento excepcional sobre la vida y las voces de la población racializada de Luisiana a principios del siglo XX. Entre los testimonios figuran los de un antiguo policía y una vecina que relata historias sobre una figura legendaria de Nueva Orleans. Aunque el folclorista Alan Lomax registró fragmentos de canciones en criollo en zonas rurales de Luisiana en 1934 y 1937, las grabaciones de Turner son los únicos registros sonoros extensos de una época en la que la lengua todavía se hablaba ampliamente. También son las únicas grabaciones conocidas de la variedad de Nueva Orleans, donde el criollo dejó de hablarse hacia la década de 1950. Esta lengua toma gran parte de su vocabulario del francés, pero cuenta con una gramática y una estructura propias , además de palabras y expresiones características. recent_candidates.title: Hallan uno de los meteoritos más antiguos de Marte
recent_candidates.author: Sinc
recent_candidates.excerpt: En 2022 se halló un meteorito de color rosa en el desierto del Sáhara y nadie sabía qué antigüedad tenía ni de dónde procedía. No fue hasta que un equipo de científicos lo dató que supo que aquella roca de casi 800 gramos era un fragmento de Marte formado hace más de 4 mil millones de años. Este hallazgo representa uno de los meteoritos marcianos más antiguos jamás encontrados. Lo nombraron Teghaza 001 , en honor a la llanura salina de Malí donde fue descubierto. Actualmente, este meteorito es uno de los 435 ejemplares que proceden de nuestro planeta vecino. Con él, los investigadores de un estudio, publicado en Science, ofrecieron una imagen excepcional de la corteza marciana. En concreto, creen que estos resultados podrían ayudar a responder muchas preguntas, entre ellas cómo interactuaban el agua y las rocas en el planeta rojo. Un estudio cartografía cómo se propaga el virus del herpes en la piel Marcos D. Oliveros «No fue hasta que empezamos a examinarlo de cerca cuando nos dimos cuenta de que este meteorito es único», expresó la autora principal del artículo, Yang Liu, del Laboratorio de Propulsión a Chorro de la NASA. «Uno de los revisores del artículo lo calificó como la Piedra de Rosetta de Marte». De color rosa A diferencia de sus homólogos, Teghaza 001 presenta una mezcla de minerales ígneos que expone cómo se formó la corteza del planeta a partir del enfriamiento del magma, antes de que fuera alterada por el agua subterránea.
